title: Fourier concentration for bounded-width DNF
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional sign cube to the two signs. Suppose $f$ has a disjunctive normal form of width at most $w$, where $w$ is a positive integer. For any real number $\varepsilon$ with $0<\varepsilon\le 1$, the sum of squared Fourier coefficients of the real-valued version of $f$ over subsets of coordinates of size greater than $30w\lceil\log_2(3/\varepsilon)\rceil$ is at most $\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a sign-valued Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$f$ has a DNF representation of width at most $w$
